text.aria-label: Subtitle text 'Spread calibration (post hoc) multiplies how far each ensemble member sits from the ensemble mean by a factor chosen per series from earlier forecast runs only, so the ensemble mean and the MAE do not change. Scored only on the 45 forecast runs after the first 8, which are left out while history builds up; 53 weekly ECMWF ensemble (ENS) forecast runs, scored from July 2025 to June 2026; seed 0. Panels a use the two arms named in the panel titles; the second arm combines absolute-error loss, early stopping, the lead-time column, lean wind columns, and one model per type with a site identifier. In panel a, a dot is the share of outcomes that fell inside the ensemble's 10% to 90% band; a well-spread ensemble sits on the dashed 80% line. In panel b, a dot is the paired difference in CRPS (calibrated minus uncalibrated), and a line is the 95% interval from resampling whole months; zero means no change.'
text.tspan: Spread calibration (post hoc) multiplies how far each ensemble member sits from the ensemble mean by a factor
chosen per series from earlier forecast runs only, so the ensemble mean and the MAE do not change.
Scored only on the 45 forecast runs after the first 8, which are left out while history builds up; 53 weekly ECMWF
ensemble (ENS) forecast runs, scored from July 2025 to June 2026; seed 0. Panels a use the two arms named in the
panel titles; the second arm combines absolute-error loss, early stopping, the lead-time column, lean wind columns,
and one model per type with a site identifier.
In panel a, a dot is the share of outcomes that fell inside the ensemble's 10% to 90% band; a well-spread ensemble
sits on the dashed 80% line. In panel b, a dot is the paired difference in CRPS (calibrated minus uncalibrated),
and a line is the 95% interval from resampling whole months; zero means no change.
